items.title: Bela Fleck interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, December 7, 2004
items.q: Victor spinning the bass... we more and more want to make sure the music is soulful and meaningful to us... Victor sings... Victor and Future Man, the Wooten brothers... they had a big deal at a certain point on Arista records

ctx.x: Is there a danger in using electronics or great sounding reverbs and stuff? Because you fall in love with the reverb rather than the music.

Yeah. Sure. But I mean unless you use it as part of what makes you create that music. Like for instance Victor does things with the JamMan Looper. And that’s technical thing, but what he does with it is so musical that by the end of it it’s — it used to strike me that way as being like a technical, like being — it was never cheesy but to me it was less interesting than hearing him play when he didn’t use the looper. But as he just stuck with it and years went by, gradually he developed these things that were like…
Learned to do really interesting things that I really like. So sometimes using an effect can launch you into a whole other musical place.
